The quotient f=|adj A|^2/Q^3 is comparable to d^2/Q and smooth on all Q>0, not a globally smooth equivalent of d.
A ten-dimensional homogeneous lift bounds the signed Hessian chain measure by the existing Frobenius measure; its zero-set remainder satisfies |sigma_f|<=K zeta_A.

Lf has finite total variation; full-cell and fixed smooth-test integrals are BV. Uniform positive mass yields a unique finite nonnegative weak-star measure trace as t approaches a finite candidate endpoint.
A compatible periodic divergence-free initial velocity realizes negative pointwise normalized viscous density, excluding an automatic nonnegative-density claim.

No strong L1 endpoint trace, absolute continuity of the weak measure trace, exclusion of concentration or finite-measure assertion for partial_t f.
